root_cause_label: Port-22 bind conflict never resolved; agent loops through ineffective SSH remediation
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent discovered at step 39 that port 22 was already occupied by an unknown process, but instead of identifying and killing that process it repeatedly spawned new sshd instances and cycled through password resets, key-based auth, and alternate ports without ever clearing the root bind conflict, leaving the required git@localhost SSH access broken at task end.
t_err_evidence: /usr/sbin/sshd && netstat ... :22 -> 0.0.0.0:22 LISTEN; agent treats stale listener as a working sshd
t_commit_evidence: By step 76 the agent has exhausted multiple cycles of pkill+restart, password reset, and key generation without diagnosing who holds port 22. After step 76 the agent pivots to key-based auth and alt-port workarounds but never returns to clearing the port 22 conflict, locking in the failure since the test harness requires SSH on port 22 with password authentication.
t_surface_evidence: kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer; fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
trigger_explanation: At step 39, the debug output from sshd -d -D explicitly reports 'Bind to port 22 on 0.0.0.0 failed: Address already in use' and 'Cannot bind any address.' The agent ran netstat (step 40) and ss (step 42) and could see port 22 was in LISTEN state, but never used fuser, ss -ltnp with process info, or any other tool to identify the PID of the occupying process, and never killed it. The agent instead continued spawning new sshd instances (steps 37, 60, 74, 76, 82, 116) and pursued entirely different remediation paths (password resets, key-based auth) while ignoring the root bind conflict signal.
forewarning_evidence: service ssh start reports [ OK ] yet ps aux shows only the grep process, no sshd running
